title: No connected graph with at most ten vertices is an unweighted death-Birth amplifier of weak selection: an exhaustive census, and a Lean check that Richter's eleven-vertex graph is one
description:
For death-Birth (dB) updating on a connected, simple, unweighted graph with N vertices, Allen et al. showed that the fixation probability of a single mutant of fitness 1 + δ is 1/N + δ(Neff − 2)/(2N) + O(δ2), and called the graph an amplifier of weak selection if Neff > N. We enumerated every connected graph with 3 ≤ N ≤ 10 (2, 6, 21, 112, 853, 11,117, 261,080 and 11,716,571 graphs) with nauty geng (counts equal to OEIS A001349) and found none with Neff > N: every regular graph has Neff = N exactly and every other graph has Neff < N; the closest non-regular graph at N = 10 lies at least 0.0207 below N, and the closest graphs are always nearly complete (KN minus an edge, or minus a maximum matching). In Lean 4 we check that on Richter's eleven-vertex graph every rational solution of Allen's coalescence system has Neff = 2668552698098/242579025123 ≈ 11.000756 > 11. Within the weak-selection criterion for unweighted graphs, the smallest dB amplifier therefore has exactly 11 vertices. The paper includes a step-by-step account for readers outside evolutionary graph theory.

Tier split. Tier A (Lean 4.34.1, Mathlib; axioms within propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound): the theorem R11_amplifier, the uniqueness theorem eq5_unique (a positive solution of the system is the only solution), the isothermal control P11_isothermal (Neff = 11 on the quartic parent), and kernel-decided negative controls (a perturbed certificate and a wrong graph are rejected; a planted sorry and a planted axiom are caught by the axiom audit). Tier L: Allen's criterion and coalescence equations, and the step from Neff > N to amplification near r = 1 (their eq. (8)); taken as stated, not re-proved. Tier C: the census (enumeration completeness rests on geng and the OEIS count; floating-point proposals are decided by an exact integer residual bound that uses the non-negativity of the inverse of I − M; the regular graphs are solved exactly with rational arithmetic) and exact-rational sign certificates for the fixation-probability difference against K11 at four values of r (and a certified sign change in [1.00082334, 1.00082349]); the census is not kernel-checked. Tier X: finite-r numerics beyond the certified points.

Controls. Positive: complete graphs, cycles and all 1, 2, 2, 5, 4, 17, 22, 167 connected regular graphs (counts equal OEIS A005177) have Neff = N; stars have Neff = 4n/(n+1); the exact-chain slope equals (Neff − 2)/(2N) on all graphs with N ≤ 6; Richter's N = 11 and cubic N = 12 values reproduced to the printed digits. Negative: Allen's printed eq. (3) for the cycle disagrees with the exact chain in 25 of 25 cases while three other sources agree with the chain (reported neutrally; not confirmed with the authors); a planted wrong random walk and the complete graph are rejected. An unexplained discrepancy remains in Richter's printed τmax values (17.6997 vs 17.69069 here), while Neff agrees.

What this is NOT. This is mathematics of graphs and of fixation probabilities in a Moran-type model. It is not a statement about real tumours, tissues, patients or any medical application, and nothing here bears on diagnosis or treatment.

Limitations. Novelty of the exhaustive statement is unchecked beyond the papers read (Allen et al., Richter 2020 and 2022, Tkadlec et al., Hindersin & Traulsen, Kaveh et al., and for novelty only Svoboda et al. and Brewster et al.); unweighted graphs, dB updating, uniform initialisation and the first-order criterion only; the finite-r checks are not a proof for all r near 1; no independent audit (human or AI) exists, no statement lock; repository guards were not run; the tissue-like (r, d) plane of the preregistration was not attempted.
